subject: Customer notification: elevated auth failures — SOC2/SIG evidence request and post-incident summary
messages:
From: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@fincobank.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: secops@fincobank.com
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected auth failures observed — request for IRP and telemetry

Hi Kimberly,

We saw a ~12-minute window this morning (08:40–08:52 PDT) where a subset of token validation calls from FinCo to your hosted API returned 401/429 spikes. No funds moved and no PII accessed, but our security team wants an incident notification and a snapshot of auth logs and telemetry for our SOC2 audit.

Can you please confirm:
- Whether Redwood saw an upstream auth anomaly at that time
- A short impact statement for our auditors (we need something we can include in our SOC2 evidence pack)
- A package (sanitized) with request/response logs, rate-limit traces, and any relevant runbook items you followed

We also want to map any delivered artifacts to the SIG/CAIQ questions (FinCo will file this under our vendor attestation). Ideally a one-day turnaround.

Thanks — we appreciate the quick response.

Lisa Chen
Senior Security Manager, FinCo Bank
lisa.chen@fincobank.com
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123

I'll reply to FinCo to confirm receipt and provide an ETA (aiming EOD PDT).

Kimberly

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com

Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 09:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Unexpected auth failures observed — request for IRP and telemetry

Kimberly / team — quick update: no gateway deploys during 08:30–09:00 PDT. We had an autoscale event at ~08:41 where ephemeral workers spun up in us-west-2 to handle higher load; that correlated with increased 429s on our auth proxies for roughly 8–10 minutes while pools balanced.

I've flagged the autoscaler logs and the auth proxy metrics (CPU, conn queue length). I'll extract the relevant ranges and put them in the Drive folder Marissa will create.

-Jonas
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Unexpected auth failures observed — request for IRP and telemetry

Lisa / FinCo team — thank you for the report and patience.

Summary and impact statement (for your SOC2 packet):
- Time window observed: 2027-08-29 08:40:12–08:52:35 PDT
- Impact: transient 401/429 responses on ~0.9% of FinCo-originating requests. No data exfiltration observed; no PII or write operations were affected. No credentials were leaked.
- Root cause (summary): an autoscaling imbalance led to a short period where new auth proxy instances were not fully warmed; requests hitting those instances experienced elevated rate limiting and a small number of validation failures.

Attached artifacts (sanitized):
- forensic-telemetry-20270829.zip (includes: redacted request IDs, timestamped auth traces, rate-limit counters, CPU/queue metrics; all customer-identifying fields redacted)
- sig-caiq-mapping.xlsx (mapping of provided artifacts to SIG/CAIQ question IDs)

Actions taken and runbook reference:
- Autoscaler policy adjusted to pre-warm a subset of instances for auth-proxy (mitigation applied 08:55 PDT).
- Temporary throttle smoothing enabled between 09:00–10:00 PDT to stabilize ramps.
- Post-incident runbook updated: IR-Auth-001 (added pre-warm step + health-check gating).

We have uploaded the artifact bundle to a secure link: https://drive.redwood.com/finco/irp-evidence/2027-08-29 (link expires in 14 days).

Next steps: please confirm if the attached package meets FinCo's evidence requirements or if you'd like additional exports (e.g., sampling of full request headers for specific timestamps). We can generate a signed evidence index for auditors if required.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Security Response Lead, Redwood Inference
